name: Mocha
intro: A mocha is a latte with chocolate stirred in, topped with a cloud of whipped cream. It tastes like a warm hug: sweet and chocolatey up front, with a coffee backbone underneath. It's a treat that works as dessert or a cozy afternoon pick-me-up.
heroAlt: Engraved line illustration of a mocha with chocolate and milk

vessel.name: Large mug or latte glass
vessel.note: The coaster recipe totals about 9 oz plus whipped cream, so a 12 oz mug has room.

ingredients.note: From roughly 18 g of finely ground coffee.
Any good chocolate syrup works. Sweetness varies by brand.
Whole milk gives the creamiest result.
Lightly sweetened, from a can or whipped fresh.

equipment.alternative: Moka pot or AeroPress plus saucepan or microwave for milk

steps.title: Add the chocolate
steps.body: Pour 1 oz of chocolate syrup into the bottom of your mug. Adding it first lets the hot espresso melt and mix it in easily.
steps.tip: Warm the mug first so the syrup loosens up.

steps.title: Pull the espresso
steps.body: Pull a double shot of espresso directly onto the chocolate. The heat of the shot helps the syrup dissolve, so stir right away until it's smooth.
steps.tip: Stirring well prevents a layer of syrup stuck at the bottom.

steps.title: Steam the milk
steps.body: Steam 6 oz of milk to about 140 to 150°F with a small amount of foam. Slightly warmer than a latte works because chocolate drinks hold their sweetness, but don't scald the milk.
steps.tip: No steam wand? Heat milk gently on the stove and whisk until slightly foamy.

steps.title: Combine
steps.body: Pour the steamed milk into the chocolate espresso, holding back foam with a spoon at first and then adding it on top. Give it a gentle stir to blend everything.

steps.title: Top with whipped cream
steps.body: Add a generous swirl of whipped cream. Fresh or canned both work, and lightly sweetened is best so it doesn't become overly sugary.

steps.title: Garnish (optional)
steps.body: Finish with a drizzle of chocolate syrup or a dusting of cocoa. The aroma is part of the treat.

homeMethods.note: Brew a moka pot and mix with chocolate syrup and warm milk. Chocolate softens the coffee's rougher edges, so a moka pot works well here, though it's less concentrated than espresso.
A strong AeroPress shot stirred into chocolate and warm milk makes a very good home mocha. No crema, but chocolate hides that.
Double-strength coffee with chocolate syrup and hot milk is a cozy mocha-style drink. It tastes milder and less coffee-forward than the real thing.

tips: Taste your syrup. Some are very sweet, so you may want to adjust.
Dissolve chocolate in the espresso, not the milk, so there are no lumps.
Mocha recipes vary by café, some using melted chocolate, cocoa powder or sauce.
commonMistakes: Not stirring, leaving syrup at the bottom.
Using a weak coffee that disappears behind the chocolate.
Adding too much chocolate and losing the espresso.

variations.name: White chocolate mocha
variations.description: Swap in white chocolate sauce for a sweeter, creamier drink.

variations.name: Mint mocha
variations.description: Add a few drops of peppermint syrup for a seasonal twist.

variations.name: Iced mocha
variations.description: Mix espresso and chocolate, add cold milk and ice.

history: The name comes from the Yemeni port of Mocha, historically important in the coffee trade. How the name came to describe chocolate-and-coffee drinks is not precisely documented.

seo.title: How to Make a Mocha: Espresso, Chocolate and Steamed Milk
seo.description: Make a cozy mocha with 2 oz espresso, 1 oz chocolate syrup, 6 oz steamed milk and whipped cream, plus easy no-machine methods.
